summary: I built the core of the write-once structure in a clone of sdkgen and tested it on the README quick start for ts, go, py and c. The pieces are: a resolved, JSON-serialisable SdkDescription per target (ts/src/helpers/sdkdesc.ts); a language-neutral example representation of 7 statement kinds and 6 expression kinds, with its builders (ts/src/helpers/example.ts); a shared ReadmeQuick.ts that writes every heading and sentence once; and four syntax providers, Syntax_<lang>.ts. The four retired ReadmeQuick_<lang>.ts files are deleted. Across 19 model variations, every changed line in the four ported languages is tagged with a reason (0 UNEXPLAINED), and the 16 unported languages are byte-identical to the old output in every variation. The providers read the model 0 times, as counted by a script. They needed no idiom notes: across ts/go/py/c, 100% of the quick-start prose sentences are the same text once each provider's 4 runtime words are masked (84.6% raw, against 30.8% in the old output). All 11 catalogued quick-start issues are fixed for all four languages by the shared code. Along the way I found and fixed one more defect: the c quick start calls getenv without including <stdlib.h>, so it does not compile, and the old code fails the same way. Examples compile and run: 16/16 ts README lanes, 12/12 go README lanes, py with a pytest stand-in on 4 models, and the c DOC lane on 5/6 models. The one c failure is the root README's ReadmeTopQuick_c, which I did not port; it has the same getenv defect and fails identically on the old code. H2 (source shrinks 2x) is refuted for this section: the four-language source grows (945 to 1069 lines, 0.88x), and the projection to 20 languages is 1.66x, below the 2x threshold. H5 is only partly supported: doctor reports a ReadmeQuick_<lang> left behind by an upgrade as 'additive' with ok: true, and `target add` never prunes src/cmp. So the migration needs a doctor rule I did not build.
stopped_at: Finished, in the brief's order: (1) the description and the representation, designed against the 20 languages' output; (2) the shared quick start, the ts and go providers and the diff report; (3) the py and c providers; (4) the lanes; (5) the metrics. Also finished: the H5 probe (doctor, target add and an alias against a leftover component) and the full suite without the toolchain lanes. Not done: (a) py ran without real pytest. pytest is not installed and the brief forbids PyPI, so the generated test/test_readme_examples.py ran under harness/pyrun.py with a 10-line stand-in for pytest.skip and pytest.fail; it executed every block. (b) I fixed no doctor rule for retired components; I only measured the gap. (c) I did not port the root README quick start (ReadmeTopQuick_<lang>); it still carries the getenv defect in c and the old server and secret behaviour. (d) The language pack (dart, haskell, lean) was not generated. It takes the same fallback path as the 16 unported languages, which I checked; the pack itself was read, not run. (e) No timings were measured. (f) The REFERENCE page was not touched; it is the next agent's task.

built.what: sdkDescription(model, targetName): the resolved description, memoised per model and target and deep-copied through JSON. It is built from envName, packageName, serverVariables, isAuthActive, isAuthSuppressed, isHttpBasicAuth, resolveAuthIn/Name, entityOps, entityIdField, entityDataIdField, opRequestShape, requiredItems, requestExampleItems, matchExampleItems and sendsId. Every quick start's selection logic lives here once: the example entity, the nested entity and its parent parameter, list, load, create, update, patch and remove arguments, the create/update field choice, and chaining on the created id.

The example representation (Ent, Ref, Expr, Entry, Stmt), the builders clientBlock, listBlock, loadBlock, writeBlock and writeOps (they read only the description), uses(), the provider interface (Syntax, RuntimeWords, Scope), and the shared walker printStmts/printBlock.

The shared quick start. The lead-in is built from the steps actually written (S28), steps are numbered by a counter, and the write heading is built from the operations present (U45). The client prose names the environment variables (D25), the required server variables and the defaulted ones; the list and load sentences are filled from the provider's RuntimeWords. Precedence: a target's own ReadmeQuick_<lang>, else its Syntax_<lang>, else the old warning path.
Syntax added to OPTIONAL_COMPONENTS as null, so a target without a provider gets a debug log and no warning.

Constructs the representation must cover across all 20 (each appears in at least one language): imports derived from what the block uses (env, entities, field reads); a constructor with an options map of env reads and a nested server map (imperative put form in java, scala and swift); a hoisted declaration (c handle and err, cpp apikey, elixir handle); an op call with a match/data map or none, a cast and trailing control args; result binding; iteration; printing a record or chosen fields; error handling (try, result match, error return, errno, eval); per-write handling or unwrap; comments; typed literals (string, number, boolean, empty list, empty map, null); a field read of the created record. My representation covers all of these except: 'print chosen fields' (perl, php, rb, lua), a printed remove result (ocaml, zig), and per-write error handling distinct from attempt (zig, rust unwrap, go) — see gaps.

decisions.topic: go structure: one program versus steps
decisions.decision: go prints the shared four steps as fragments; there is no '### Quickstart' program.
decisions.why: go does not need a whole compilable unit. Its README harness (ReadmeExamplesTest_go.ts:159-196) compiles fragments by wrapping each in a function, and 18 of 20 languages use steps. The single program is drift. The go README lanes pass (12/12, including the new Basic/templated-server lane).

decisions.topic: Prose wording: one sentence per fact
decisions.decision: List: '<op> returns <many> of entities, one per record, and <fails>; <data> reads an entity's record.' Load: '<op> returns the entity and <fails>; <data> reads its record.' The 4 placeholders are the provider's RuntimeWords.

Iterate them directly...'; py: '... raises on error; ... (a `dict`)'; c: '... — check `err` after the call'). The extra clauses repeat the failure fact or restate the entity contract, so they were dropped rather than kept as idiom notes.

decisions.topic: Precedence between a target's own ReadmeQuick_<lang> and its Syntax_<lang>
decisions.decision: The own component wins; then the provider; then the old warning.
decisions.why: Provider-first would silently drop a project's fork. Component-first keeps a fork, but it also keeps an unmodified leftover from an upgrade writing the old tutorial, which doctor reports as 'additive' (h5.js). Neither is safe without a doctor rule; component-first loses nothing.

facts_that_leaked: In each case below an old per-language component held a model-dependent condition; each now sits in the description. Server variables (which are required, which defaulted): now desc.server and desc.options. No provider reads them.
Basic secret: the old ts component tested isHttpBasicAuth alone. It is now desc.auth.secret (basic, header placement, not suppressed); providers only print the options list.
Chaining on the created id: three different rules (ts type-checked, py and c unchecked, go never). Now DescArg.fromCreated, decided in sdkdesc; the go provider prints whatever it is handed.
Nested entity and parent parameter: go never chose one. Now desc.quick.load.nested.
Which write operations appear, and the create/update field choice: copied into each component. Now desc.quick.create, update, patch and remove.

Borderline, a fact derived from description strings rather than read from the model: the py provider builds its import module as `${desc.Name.toLowerCase()}_sdk`, as the old component did. That is a layout fact of the py target. It belongs in the description (a per-target `module` field), but deriving it needs language knowledge the description builder does not have; this is the clearest pressure point.

Borderline: the c provider builds its identifier stem from desc.name (`toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g,'')`), duplicating utility_c's cIdent(model). It also copies C_RESERVED and cVarName, because utility_c also exports helpers that read the model. A pure naming module per language would remove the copies.

Alias provenance: desc.package comes from packageName(model, target), which reads `origname` to know that go2 is a go target. The old go component called goModule(model, target) directly. With the model `target add go~go2` writes (origname: go) the output is the same. A hand-made alias model without origname would get 'voxgig-sdk-demo-sdk' as its go module. My first alias staging omitted origname and showed exactly this; fixed by staging as target add does.

Not a model fact but provider state across blocks: c hoists entity handles once per section, and go declares err once per block. Both are handled by Scope (declared, local, stmts), which is passed in, so the providers stay pure functions of what they are given.

tests:
Build: `npm run build` passes, including check-scaffold, check-fixture and stage-scaffold (about 5 s). Suites run: readme, helpers, agentguide, optional, readmeintro, characterize and lua-table-keys (102 tests); then generate, optional and characterize (213; 1 fail at first, fixed in the provider); then the whole suite without generatedcompile, run cleanly (2514 tests, 2508 pass, 5 skipped, 1 golden fail, then `npm run golden` and characterize 2/2 pass). One run had about 120 spurious failures of under 1 ms because I rebuilt dist while it ran; I discarded it and reran without building.

What changed and why: (1) optional.test 'the guide the warning links to lists every optional component' failed because Syntax joined OPTIONAL_COMPONENTS. I fixed the documentation (docs/how-to/author-a-new-language.md), not the test. (2) test/golden/add-output.txt was regenerated with `npm run golden`. The diff is exactly the four retired ReadmeQuick_<lang>.ts out and the four Syntax_<lang>.ts in. (3) generate.test 'a list example passes the parameters the list requires, in every target' failed when my ts provider printed a two-member list match on several lines; the test reads one following line. I fixed the provider (the list match stays inline), not the test. (4) generatedcompile.test.ts gained a BASIC_SERVER model and three kinds of lane: the ts README loop, every README_LANES lane, and the DOC_LANES models. That is how the c getenv defect was found.

Toolchain lanes run: ts README 16/16, go README 12/12, c DOC 5/6 (the one failure is the unported root README, and it fails on OLD as well). The py lane was not runnable (no pytest); its README example test ran under a stand-in instead. No test file was weakened.
gaps: The representation has no statement for printing CHOSEN fields of a record. perl prints ->{id}, php and rb print id and radius, lua prints rec["id"]. Today that choice is made inside those components; it needs a description field (which fields to show) and an Expr form for it.
A remove's result is shown by ocaml (`removed.e_deleted`) and zig ('removed'); there is no Stmt for 'show the deleted marker'.

Per-write error handling distinct from attempt (zig wraps each write in a switch, rust unwraps, go checks): go handles it inside call. zig would need either attempt around each write or a per-call handling mode; the builder emits writes without attempt.
Options built imperatively (java, scala and swift use put or entries) are printable from the same Entry list. Not tried.
Imports that depend on the entities used (clojure requires the entity namespace) are supported through uses(stmts), but no provider exercised it.
js's 'Direct API Access' section and its other drift are undecided; it is a how-to section living in the tutorial.
The description has no per-target layout facts (py import module, c identifier stem). Providers derive them from strings, which is borderline.
No retired-component rule in doctor: a ReadmeQuick_<lang> left by an upgrade is 'additive', so a migration cannot be reported or pruned (H5).
server-none: the description says nothing about `base` (the URL a spec without servers needs); the quick start shows no option.
The root README quick start (ReadmeTopQuick_<lang>) is still per-language, with the same S49, S50, G01 and M12 issues and the c getenv defect.
RuntimeWords are English fragments chosen to fit two sentence frames. A third sentence frame may need more words, and the interface would grow.
surprises: The source grew for four languages (0.88x). The fixed cost of the description, the representation and the walker (about 650 lines) only pays back across many languages, and even 20 projects to 1.66x. Most of the old per-language code was selection logic that already called shared helpers; per language it was not as large as the brief's 36,000-line figure suggests for the whole documentation.

The c quick start never compiled with auth active (getenv without <stdlib.h>). Nothing caught it, because the DOC-lane models have auth off. The root README copy has the same defect, which illustrates the proposal's own point.
The go README harness compiles fragments, so go's whole-program form was a choice, not a need. No language among the four needs a compilable unit.
doctor's `known` check consults only the current scaffold, not the copy record. A component the scaffold stops shipping becomes 'additive (project-owned)', the same as a deliberate project extension.
packageName for an alias depends on `origname` in the target's model, while the old go component used goModule directly, so the description inherits a provenance dependency.
Masking the 4 runtime words makes 100% of the prose identical across four languages. The old prose was only 30.8% identical, and none of its extra clauses held a fact the others lacked.
Three interface changes were needed by the second and fourth providers (go err scoping, c lookahead and hoisting), all about cross-statement state rather than syntax of one statement.

hypotheses.evidence: Supported for the four ported languages, not tested for the other 16. Providers read the model 0 times (script count). Per-language prose that cannot be shared is 0% (100% shared once 4 runtime words are masked; 0 idiom notes), well under the 15% threshold. Interface changes after the first provider: 3, one of them breaking, under the threshold of about 10. Untested: the survey shows constructs the representation lacks for perl, php, rb, lua, ocaml and zig (chosen-field printing, a printed remove result, per-write handling), so more additive changes are expected. Whether those stay out of providers depends on putting 'which fields to print' in the description.

Four languages: 945 to 1069 lines (0.88x, a growth). Projection to 20: 4537 to 2729 (1.66x), below the 2x threshold, assuming the other 16 providers average the four measured (103.75 lines; c alone is 142). Command: node harness/metrics.js.

All 11 catalogued quick-start issues (S28, U45, S49, S50, G01, M13, M14, D23, D55, M12, D25) are fixed for ts, go, py and c, shown on B, crud-noupdate, auth-basic, auth-basic-query and server-mixed. Ten are fixed by shared code; M14 is fixed by the go provider's single member printer, so no per-language EDIT was needed for any of them. D23, D55, M12 and D25 are fixed only in the quick start; their other sites (ReadmeModel, ReadmeRef, ReadmeHowto, ReadmeTop, go-cli) are outside this section. One new defect (c getenv) needed a provider edit, which is a syntax fact.

ts README lanes 16/16, go README lanes 12/12, py README test on 4 models with a pytest stand-in (all blocks executed), c DOC lane 5/6. The c failure is in the unported root README and fails identically on the OLD clone; the ported c section compiles on basic-server where OLD did not. No failure is intrinsic to the approach.

Supported: aliases (go~go2 copies Syntax_go2.ts; the alias variation generates through it); unported and packaged targets keep their own components through the fallback (272 unported READMEs byte-identical); the golden and doctor are clean on a fresh project. Not safe as built (node harness/h5.js): target add never prunes src/cmp, and doctor reports a leftover ReadmeQuick_<lang> as additive with ok: true. With component-first precedence the leftover silently keeps the old tutorial; with provider-first a real fork would be silently dropped. It looks fixable within doctor's rules: a retired-components list beside `superseded`, or using the copy record's fingerprint to tell a pristine leftover from a fork. I did not build it. The language pack was not generated (read, not run).

handoff:
Everything is under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f1977c62-4748-5872-8f72-6f448dbac3f1/scratchpad/design/proto2/core/. The clone is sdkgen/ (commits f21e6fe1..950912e7 on 9aebaf9e); the harness is harness/ (README.txt lists the commands); stored outputs are in harness/out/{old,new}/<variation>/<target>/README.md.

For the REFERENCE page: extend SdkDescription (ts/src/helpers/sdkdesc.ts) rather than reading the model in the shared component. desc.entities already carries ops, id, dataId and parents per active entity; add the per-op argument lists the REFERENCE shows (requiredItems, matchExampleItems, requestExampleItems are the helpers) and the option rows. Reuse desc.options and desc.server for the constructor table, so S49, S50, G01 and M12 close there too. Find a provider with optionalComponent(ctx$, target, 'Syntax'). A section with a provider writes every sentence itself, conditioned on the description; a target with no provider must stay byte-identical (check it with harness/diff.js, adapting qsect.js to the REFERENCE section).

Rules a provider follows: pure functions of (statement or expression, desc, scope); no model, no ctx$, no import of utility_<lang> or @voxgig/apidef; only the pure helpers (exampleVarName, jsKey, jsProp, jsQuote, camelify, indentLines). It decides HOW, never WHETHER. Anything that decides whether a thing is shown goes in the description or the builder. State across blocks goes in Scope: declared is per section, local per block, stmts is the current block. Runtime facts the prose needs go in RuntimeWords, as phrases that fit the shared sentences. harness/metrics.js counts violations; keep it at 0.

Watch for: (1) the survey's open constructs (chosen-field printing in perl, php, rb and lua; the printed remove result in ocaml and zig; per-write handling in zig and rust) need representation additions and a description field for the field choice; do not let a provider pick fields. (2) py's import module and c's identifier stem are derived in providers from desc strings; add per-target layout fields if a language needs more. (3) H5 is not closed: doctor needs a retired-components rule before a release could retire ReadmeQuick_<lang> for existing projects. ReadmeQuick.ts currently lets a project's own ReadmeQuick_<lang> win over its provider. (4) Alias packages depend on origname; stage aliases as target add writes them (harness/gen.js stageAlias). (5) The c DOC lane with auth active fails on ReadmeTopQuick_c (getenv without stdlib.h); port or patch it with the root quick start. (6) No pytest here: use harness/pylane.js. (7) Never rebuild dist while a suite runs; it produces about 120 spurious sub-millisecond failures.

For porters of the other 16: copy the shape of Syntax_ts.ts (simplest) or Syntax_c.ts (hoisting, lookahead). Expect structure decisions like go's to be counted in diff.js reasons, and add reason rules to diff.js rather than leaving UNEXPLAINED. Each port should also delete ReadmeQuick_<lang>.ts and refresh the golden (`npm run golden`).
